To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the liver is an important site of inflammation during sepsis and that hepatic inflammation can be modulated by the administration of an anti-inflammatory agent, such as IL-10.

hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury is a complex process involving multiple pathways and that there is a need for more research to understand the role of these different pathways in hepatic ischemia reperfusion injury.
hepatic venous occlusions cause more damage after reperfusion in a murine hepatic ischemia/reperfusion model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of hepatic venous clamping on hepatic ischemia/reperfusion injury.
the effect of hepatic venous clamping on the liver during liver surgery.
the effects of portal clamping on liver function and hepatic microcirculation in an experimental model of liver resection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a liver retraction system in liver surgery is safe and feasible.
the use of portal clamping is superior to HVO in terms of postoperative outcome and liver function in a murine liver surgery model.
hepatic venous clamping should be avoided in liver surgery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury is a multifactorial process that involves the activation of the immune system and that the hepatic venous outflow is more important than portal inflow in the pathophysiology of ischemia-reperrifusion injury.

we developed a new method for measuring hepatic venous flow, and that the results of this study show that hepatic venous occlusions are more harmful to liver function after reperfusion, compared to portal clamping.
the liver is more sensitive to ischemic injury when venous outflow is occluded compared with when portal inflow is interrupted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is an organ with high metabolic activity, and the liver is the only organ that can regenerate itself.
the use of the liver as a source for stem cells is feasible, and that the liver can be used to treat liver diseases.
the liver can be resected safely with the help of a robotic system.
